{{Puzzles |Lists}}
This is a list of [[puzzle]]s that cannot be solved. An impossible puzzle is a puzzle that cannot be resolved, either due to lack of sufficient information, or any number of [[logical]] impossibilities.

* [[15 Puzzle]] – Slide fifteen numbered tiles into numerical order. It is impossible to solve in half of the starting positions.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Archer |first=Aaron F. |date=November 1999 |title=A Modern Treatment of the 15 Puzzle |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/00029890.1999.12005124 |journal=The American Mathematical Monthly |language=en |volume=106 |issue=9 |pages=793–799 |doi=10.1080/00029890.1999.12005124 |issn=0002-9890}}</ref>
* [[Five room puzzle]] – Cross each wall of a diagram exactly once with a continuous line.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bakst |first=Aaron |last2=Gardner |first2=Martin |date=May 1962 |title=The Second Scientific American Book of Mathematical Puzzles and Diversions. |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.2307/2312171 |journal=The American Mathematical Monthly |volume=69 |issue=5 |pages=455 |doi=10.2307/2312171 |issn=0002-9890}}</ref>
* [[MU puzzle]] – Transform the string {{mono|MI}} to {{mono|MU}} according to a set of rules.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Hofstadter |first=Douglas R. |title=Gödel, Escher, Bach: an eternal golden braid |date=1999 |publisher=Basic Books |isbn=978-0-394-75682-0 |edition=20th anniversary |location=New York}}</ref>
* [[Mutilated chessboard problem]] – Place 31 dominoes of size 2×1 on a chessboard with two opposite corners removed.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Starikova |first=Irina |last2=Paul |first2=Jean |last3=Bendegem |first3=Van |date=2020 |title=Revisiting the mutilated chessboard or the many roles of a picture |url=http://rgdoi.net/10.13140/RG.2.2.31980.80007 |journal=Logique et Analyse|language=en |doi=10.13140/RG.2.2.31980.80007}}</ref>
* Coloring the edges of the [[Petersen graph#Coloring|Petersen graph]] with three colors.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Holton |first=Derek Allan |title=The Petersen graph |last2=Sheehan |first2=J. |date=1993 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-43594-9 |series=Australian Mathematical Society lecture series |location=Cambridge [England]}}</ref>
* [[Seven Bridges of Königsberg]] – Walk through a city while crossing each of seven bridges exactly once.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Euler |first=Leonhard |date=1953 |title=Leonhard Euler and the Koenigsberg Bridges |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/24944279 |journal=Scientific American |volume=189 |issue=1 |pages=66–72 |issn=0036-8733}}</ref>
* [[Squaring the circle]], the impossible problem of constructing a square with the same area as a given circle, using only a [[compass and straightedge]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kasner |first=Edward |date=1933 |title=Squaring the Circle |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/15685 |journal=The Scientific Monthly |volume=37 |issue=1 |pages=67–71 |issn=0096-3771}}</ref>
* [[Three cups problem]] – Turn three cups right-side up after starting with one wrong and turning two at a time.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Sanford |first=A. J. |title=The mind of man: models of human understanding |date=1987 |publisher=Yale University Press |isbn=978-0-300-03960-3 |location=New Haven}}</ref>
* [[Three utilities problem]] – Connect three cottages to gas, water, and electricity without crossing lines.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kullman |first=David E. |date=November 1979 |title=The Utilities Problem |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/0025570X.1979.11976807 |journal=Mathematics Magazine |language=en |volume=52 |issue=5 |pages=299–302 |doi=10.1080/0025570X.1979.11976807 |issn=0025-570X}}</ref>
* [[Thirty-six officers problem]] – Arrange six regiments consisting of six officers each of different ranks in a 6 × 6 square so that no rank or regiment is repeated in any row or column.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Huczynska |first=Sophie |date= October 2006 |title=Powerline communication and the 36 officers problem |url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rsta.2006.1885 |journal=Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A: Mathematical, Physical and Engineering Sciences |language=en |volume=364 |issue=1849 |pages=3199–3214 |doi=10.1098/rsta.2006.1885 |issn=1364-503X}}</ref>
